verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. Harbor recorded binary_reward 0 [1], and the held-out evaluator ran the submitted `/app/solver.py` on the baked-in training HDF5 (100×101×1024 fields), reporting nRMSE 0.073640, continuous reward 0.404400, and LegacySuccess False—well above the instruction's pass bar of nRMSE below 0.0125 [2][3] and below the verifier's binary collapse threshold of reward > 0.800 [4]. The agent spent ~45 minutes implementing a WENO5-HLLC finite-volume solver with implicit viscous splitting, but its validation never touched the official reference data: at startup `/app` was empty aside from logs [5], and all accuracy claims rested on synthetic coarse-versus-fine grid self-tests that reported velocity nRMSE around 0.0023 at N=64 and 0.0017 at N=128 [6][7]. On that basis it concluded the solver was complete and validated [8], yet when the verifier applied the same nRMSE metric against the true high-fidelity trajectories the error was roughly six times the required tolerance [2][3]. The solver is a substantive numerical attempt, not a stub or cheat, but it did not genuinely meet the task's accuracy requirement, so TN is the right classification.
